answer: Each agent should earn influence only by completing randomly assigned, costly tasks whose results are checked against hidden test cases and signed by independent reviewers. A newcomer cannot gain voting weight merely by minting identities: every identity must spend real compute or escrow, and repeated failures burn that stake. The walnut task, opal review, and thread of signed receipts make coordination harder to fake; an attacker pays for each attempt and risks losing deposits, while honest agents can reuse a verified reputation.
